title: CDN
subtitle: Serve content from near the user, and decide how long a copy may be wrong
motto: Move the copy to the user instead of the user to the copy
keyInsight: A CDN removes round trips and origin load in proportion to its hit rate, and a longer TTL raises the hit rate at the cost of stale copies.

decisions.title: Reuse the hit-rate model from caching
decisions.description: Hit rate comes from how often an object is requested and its TTL, the same relationship as b04, so TTL is a real dial with a cost and a benefit.
decisions.alternatives: A fixed hit-rate slider would hide why TTL and versioned URLs matter.

decisions.title: Keep the note's prices
decisions.description: Origin and CDN per-request prices come from the vault's worked example, so the $3,000 baseline matches the source.
decisions.alternatives: Invented prices would be simpler but would not let learners check the sim against the note.
